questions.text:
Consider the relations r(A, B) and s(B, C), where s.B is a primary key and r.B is a foreign key referencing s.B. Consider the query
[latex]Q:r \Join (\sigma _{B\lt 5}(s))[/latex]
Let LOJ denote the natural left outer-join operation. Assume that r and s contain no null values.
Which one of the following queries is NOT equivalent to Q?
questions.solution:
Q keeps only r-tuples whose B value is [latex]\lt[/latex] 5 (joined with s).
Option 3, [latex]r\ LOJ\ \sigma_{B \lt 5}(s)[/latex], also keeps r-tuples with B [latex]\ge[/latex] 5, padded with NULLs, so it returns extra rows [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not equivalent.

The others filter on B [latex]\lt[/latex] 5, and since every r.B exists in s (foreign key), the outer joins add nothing.

Answer: [latex]r\ LOJ\ (\sigma_{B \lt 5}(s))[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following two tables and four queries in SQL.

Which one of the queries above is certain to have an output that is a superset of the outputs of the other three queries?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Query 1 (inner join): matching rows only.
- Query 2 (left outer): matching rows + unmatched Book rows.
- Query 3 (right outer): matching rows + unmatched Stock rows.
- Query 4 (full outer): matching rows + unmatched rows from both sides, so it always contains the other three.

Answer: Query 4

questions.text:
In an Entity-Relationship (ER) model, suppose R is a many-to-one relationship from entity set E1 to entity set E2. Assume that E1 and E2 participate totally in R and that the cardinality of E1 is greater than the cardinality of E2.
Which one of the following is true about R?
questions.solution:
Many-to-one from E1 to E2 means each E1 entity relates to at most one E2 entity; total participation of E1 makes it at least one. So every E1 entity is associated with exactly one E2 entity. Since E1 is larger, E2 entities may have several E1 partners.

Answer: Every entity in E1 is associated with exactly one entity in E2

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Every entity in E1 is associated with exactly one entity in E2.
Some entity in E1 is associated with more than one entity in E2.
Every entity in E2 is associated with exactly one entity in E1.
Every entity in E2 is associated with at most one entity in E1.

questions.text: A B-Tree used as an index for a large database table has four levels including the root node. If a new key is inserted in this index, then the maximum number of nodes that could be newly created in the process are
questions.solution:
In the worst case the insertion splits the leaf and every node on the path up to the root: 4 levels give 4 new nodes from the splits, plus 1 new root, so 5.

Answer: 5

questions.text: Which of these is characteristic of RAID 5?
questions.solution:
RAID 5 uses block-level striping with parity distributed across all disks (RAID 4 has a dedicated parity disk; RAID 6 has double parity).

Answer: Distributed parity
